title: Cataract Plus a Tired Macula

patient.name: Mr Raj Anand
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for PAM before cataract surgery — cataract with known macular degeneration

history.hpc: Mr Raj says 'My eye blur and the centre also got a dark patch, doctor say my macula not so good.' He has a cataract but also known age-related macular degeneration. The doctor ordered a PAM to estimate how much the cataract surgery alone could improve his vision.
history.pmhx: Cataract with co-existing dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD).
history.social_hx: Retired. Uses a magnifier to read.

examination_findings.fundus: Macular drusen and pigmentary changes noted by the doctor

pam.result_right: Predicted potential acuity around 6/60 — poor potential
pam.interpretation: Poor predicted acuity suggests the macular disease limits the benefit of cataract surgery; flagged for the doctor

diagnosis: PAM completed after dilation. The predicted potential acuity is poor (around 6/60), consistent with the known macular degeneration limiting the visual benefit of cataract surgery. The OT reports the limited predicted outcome to the doctor for counselling and does not make the surgical decision.

immediate: Confirm identity and the correct eye against the order
Explain the test simply and position the patient
Obtain the best predicted acuity and repeat to confirm
Flag the poor predicted result clearly for the doctor
Record the predicted acuity and the co-existing macular history
follow_up: Doctor to counsel the patient that macular disease may limit improvement
Consider macular imaging (e.g. OCT) for fuller assessment
patient_education: Explain the test estimates how much surgery alone could help
Avoid over-promising — the doctor will discuss realistic expectations
Explain dilation will blur near vision for a few hours

key_points: Confirms identity and the correct eye
Confirms dilation as required for PAM
Notes the co-existing macular disease as relevant
Explains the purpose of the test
Sets up and performs PAM correctly
Understands PAM estimates the benefit of cataract surgery
Links poor potential to the macular disease
Does not make the surgical decision — reports to the doctor
Knows further macular imaging may be useful
Flags the poor predicted outcome to the doctor
Documents the result and macular history
